results: MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: restricted diffusion consistent with a lacunar infarct
blood glucose: 30.63 mmol/L (551.3 mg/dL) with glycosuria and NO ketonuria
HbA1c: very high on admission; 5.73% at first follow-up once glucose was controlled
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute ischaemic stroke – lacunar infarct of the contralateral subthalamic nucleus causing hemiballismus, secondary to hypertensive small vessel disease

Alternatives:
1. Hyperglycaemic hemichorea–hemiballismus (diabetic striatopathy) precipitated by severe non-ketotic hyperglycaemia
2. Small deep (subthalamic) intracerebral haemorrhage
3. Other structural lesion of the subthalamic region (e.g., tumour, demyelination, abscess)
order_raw:
1. MRI brain with diffusion-weighted imaging
